newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dollar vols jump in Europe as spot surges.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols jump in Europe as spot surges.

text.p: Dollar option volatilities climbed higher in European trade, boosted by dollar spot's fresh highs against the mark and its continued uptrend on the yen and sterling.
Dealers said dollar/mark's break above 1.87 Tuesday and then up to 1.89 today -- its highest levels since October 1989 -- prompted a flurry of options activity as options players scrambled for cover.

"The break above 1.87 flushed out a lot of reluctant buyers at the front-end," said a UK bank dealer. "There's been ongoing dollar call buying in the far-dates but this latest surge has seen this come in to the near-dates."

One-month dollar/mark volatility stood at 11.8/12.2 percent against 10.7/11.0 late Tuesday. The risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility between calls relative to puts, shifted its bias deeper towards mark puts to 0.8/1.1 from 0.5/0.8 Tuesday.
Dealers said demand for the low-delta dollar calls continued with strikes at 1.90, 2.00 and above still popular and in size.
"We're seeing the longer-term players picking these up now, the short-term speculative people have really been sitting on the sidelines on this latest rally," said U.S. bank options broker.
